CHANGES CONJUNCT RE-GRADED 2026-09-22: MET ON ONE PATH ONLY, NOT MET ON THE SHIPPED DEFAULT. The conjunct audit recorded CHANGES as MET on the construct from #672 -- a per-user slot served from cache only while fresh, falling through to a credentialed refetch once aged out. That is a TIME-based staleness mechanism. It self-corrects eventually; it does not isolate at the moment the authorization context changes, which is what the clause asks for. The question the audit did not put is what the per-user slot is KEYED on, and the answer differs by propagation strategy because TWO functions named cache_binding exist and either may produce PropagatedCredential::cache_binding, which is what PoolKey::PerUser { binding } carries (pool.rs:42-44). PATH A, NOT MET -- identity_propagation::cache_binding(subject_key, audience) at identity_propagation/mod.rs:316 takes no grant input at all, and subject_key is stable_actor_id(), which is format!("oidc:{issuer}:{subject}") at key_server/oidc.rs:132-140 and therefore STABLE ACROSS A GRANT ROTATION BY DESIGN. Produced at identity_propagation/mod.rs:460. So a slot populated under one grant and still inside its freshness window is served to the same caller after a rotation, carrying the predecessor's catalogue under the successor's grant. No race and no in-flight fill are required; this is the steady state. PropagationStrategyKind::SignedAssertion is documented at identity_propagation/mod.rs:207-209 as "the reference strategy shipped in this slice", so this is the default configuration rather than an exotic one. PATH B, MET -- personal_accounts::vault::cache_binding(account, lease) at vault.rs:311 composes the binding from the account digest plus lease.generation, lease.authorization_epoch, lease.token_revision and lease.descriptor_revision, and is produced at vault.rs:269. A rotation mints a different binding, hence a different PoolKey, so the successor cannot reach the predecessor's slot; a revoked grant yields no lease and therefore no binding to look up. On this path the isolation is a property of key construction rather than of eviction, which is stronger than a test. CONSEQUENCE: this row now has TWO unmet conjuncts, not one. Closing it requires the REVOCATION work already tracked as MIK-7530 AND making the signed-assertion binding grant-aware, or otherwise invalidating the per-user slot on a grant change for that strategy. MIK-7530's retirement construct therefore fires on ROTATION as well as revocation; both earlier revisions of its test plan described it as a revocation-only construct, which is an under-specification that every revocation-only cell would have passed. THE CREDITED TEST EVIDENCE EXERCISES ONLY THE UNMET PATH, AND LABELS NEITHER. Verified at source 2026-09-22 in the suite shipped by #666, src/gateway/meta_mcp/catalogue_per_caller_tests.rs: it configures PropagationStrategyKind::SignedAssertion at :177 and :513, and installs a test strategy whose binding is format!("{subject_key}@{}", backend.audience) at :53 -- grant-unaware, faithfully mirroring the real signed-assertion binding. So the suite backing the per-caller conjuncts runs exclusively on the path that is NOT rotation-aware, with a double that reproduces precisely the property at issue, and states nowhere which strategy it covers. It could not have detected this gap by construction, and a reader finds a passing per-caller suite and reasonably concludes both paths are covered. BY CONTRAST the vault path documents its rotation-awareness as a deliberate design property, vault.rs:305-310: "the grant authority the credential was released under: a re-authorized or rotated account produces a different binding, so a result cached for the previous grant is never served for the new one." One path states the property and implements it; the other implements neither and is the shipped default; and the tests cover only the second. CONSEQUENCE FOR GRADING: every per-caller cell in this row's evidence must name the strategy it configures. A cell that does not is untestable as written, because the two bindings give opposite answers to the same question, and silence reads as "both considered" when it means "one was run". This applies to MIK-7530's acceptance rows and retroactively to the #666 suite, which should gain the label even where its verdict does not change.
PROVENANCE: found by the agent that wrote the conjunct audit, when asked what evidence would make it doubt a test row it had twice asserted was green. It cited only the first cache_binding; the two-path scoping above is the correction to that, verified at source here. Recorded rather than quietly amended because the audit's MET grade for this conjunct has been quoted in a merged PR body and in two review packets.

DESCOPE DECLINED 2026-09-22, dual-reviewed, on grounds that need no new operator ruling. WHAT IS DECLINED, precisely: the claim that an unused implementation DISCHARGES the revocation obligation. GROUND 1, ALREADY RULED. The release owner declined this argument for this row and ruled BUILD. The ruling is in source at src/gateway/meta_mcp/catalogue_isolation_tests.rs:12-14, whose module comment states the criterion, names PR #604 as the declined rescope, and calls its own cases the acceptance edge of that ruling. The same reclassification was then made independently for MIK-6744.STORE.2 on 2026-09-20, whose note records the identical basis -- that 4.0.0 ships no production revoke path -- and calls it WRONG.
GROUND 2, PREMISE FALSE ON THE APPROVED TEXT. The descope rests on the expect(dead_code) reason at src/personal_accounts/mod.rs:518-524 and src/personal_accounts/service.rs:319-325, both reading "per-user OAuth scaffolding, deferred to post-4.0.0 backlog MIK-6744/6745/6746". That annotation does not merely lag the scope update, it CONTRADICTS it: git dates it to commit d47e1ae5 on 2026-09-12, six days AFTER the 2026-09-06 scope update pulled those tickets in. RELEASE-4.0.0-scope-update.md:7-9 supersedes the deferral of MIK-6744/6745; line 43 requires of STORE.2 that "Revocation and restart preserve credential isolation"; line 44 requires of JOURNEY.1 that the Open WebUI journey complete "connect, use, refresh, revoke and cancelled-consent". The clause has a domain.
THE TRIGGER IS UNOWNED, which is the finding both reviewers converged on and the reason this note supersedes an earlier draft that assumed STORE.2 would supply it. STORE.2's own note scopes its remaining work to three specified tests (conjunct 3 coverage, conjunct 2 oracle, conjunct 2 crash point); none adds a production revoke entry point. So no row in this release currently owns wiring a production revoke trigger, and saying the conjunct is blocked on STORE.2 would have parked it behind work that was never going to deliver it.
THE GAP IS TWO CONSTRUCTS, NOT ONE. CORRECTED 2026-09-22 -- an earlier revision of this note said the invalidation mechanism already existed and only a trigger was missing. That was half right and the wrong half was load-bearing, so it is restated here rather than quietly edited. WHAT EXISTS: MetaMcp::set_identity_grants at src/gateway/meta_mcp/mod.rs:1286-1294 replaces the grant store and bumps a monotonic policy epoch while the write lock is still held, with a debug_assert refusing a reset, and policy_epoch_tests.rs:51 proves a pre-change entry cannot be served afterwards. Its one production caller is src/gateway/server/mod.rs:1239. WHAT THAT DOES NOT REACH: the epoch keys RESULT-cache entries only. `rg policy_epoch src/backend/` returns ZERO matches, so no catalogue or metadata cache is keyed on it. Grading MIK-7530 on the epoch alone would leave the catalogue half of scope-tests.md:40 -- "check both catalogue AND call results" -- red. SO THE ROW NEEDS BOTH: (1) a revoke path that reaches set_identity_grants, which strands result keys minted under the superseded grant; and (2) eviction of the revoked identity's pool slot, which is what drops the catalogue and metadata caches. THE OBVIOUS HOOK FOR (2) IS THE WRONG ONE, and the code already says so at src/backend/metadata.rs:57-59: invalidate_tools_cache passes Vec::is_empty to invalidate_if, so it "discards an empty list only, so routing revocation through it would be a silent no-op on every populated cache. Revocation evicts the identity's slot, which drops its transport and its caches together." That conditional is deliberate and load-bearing -- clearing unconditionally could erase a tool list another reader populated between one caller observing emptiness and acting on it. Do not weaken it; evict the slot instead. THE NEAREST EXISTING MACHINERY is PersonalAccountPool::evict_idle_per_user_entries (src/backend/pool.rs:326), which evicts per-user entries but is keyed on an idle TTL rather than on an identity. An identity-keyed eviction is the construct this conjunct is missing. A SEPARATE TRAP IN THE SAME AREA: invalidate_if (src/backend/cached_metadata.rs:140-150) returns early when a populated slot's predicate says keep, and the generation bump sits BELOW that return -- so a populated slot neither discards nor bumps. The cold-start half exists; the warm half, which is the state this row was created to produce, does not.
CLOSURE IS GRADED ON THE ACCEPTANCE TESTS, not on a hook existing: RELEASE-4.0.0-scope-tests.md:40 already specifies the discriminators -- warm-cache eviction, revocation during a fill, catalogue AND call results, and an unaffected caller as the admitted-case control. A hook wired without those is not this conjunct MET.
The stale annotation reason should be corrected by whoever wires the path. expect rather than allow means the annotation becomes a build failure the moment a caller appears, so it cannot outlive the wiring; the risk is only that its reason text is read as scope evidence meanwhile, which is exactly what happened here.

A populated per-caller slot is precisely the state this row was created to produce. THE DESCOPE QUESTION, restated because it is now a one-line ruling rather than an open problem. PR #604 argued the operative word is *supported*, so the isolation clause had nothing to range over. That argument is superseded: the clause now ranges over something and that something is isolated per caller. That reading is coherent and much better founded than #604's, because C0 through C3 are constructs rather than arguments. It is still narrowing a criterion until it is satisfied, which this row's own note records as a scope decision an agent cannot mint, so it is NOT TAKEN here. decisions.selection: Operator ruling 2026-09-20 funded four provable-agent-identity changes for 4.0.0, design review required before any code. They sat only inside the met MIK-6746.CONTRACT.1 row, so no count of remaining release work saw them. Root defect verified at source 2026-09-21: AgentIdentity (src/security/agent_identity.rs:60) uses one field for both a proven principal and a declared label; extract_agent_identity (:106-112) returns the X-Agent-ID header before reading the JWT claim, so an attacker-controlled header outranks a verified claim; the allowlist check (:161) never consults identity.source. Design in flight at docs/internal/design/2026-09-21-provable-agent-identity.md; design review, test review, failing tests, implementation and final review remain.
